requirement_text: "the applicant decides if they would like their SAT or ACT scores to be considered." "SAT and ACT scores will become part of the overall review of a student's application" if submitted. "Applicants will not be penalized or put at a disadvantage if they choose not to submit SAT or ACT scores." Self-reported scores are not accepted; official scores must come directly from the testing agency.
limitations: Page does not state which specific admission cycle/year this applies to (evergreen wording). Several third-party aggregator sites claimed USC would require testing again for the 2025-26 cycle; the official primary page directly contradicts that and was treated as authoritative per source-priority rules.
researcher_notes: Cross-referenced against admission.usc.edu/apply and admissionblog.usc.edu (same domain family) for consistency; no conflicting official-domain page found.

requirement_text: "All international applicants whose native language is not English" must submit a USC-approved English proficiency exam; "We do not grant waivers or exceptions to this policy under any circumstances." TOEFL iBT: exams before 21 Jan 2026 need "minimum score of 100 and no less than a score of 20 in each section"; exams from 21 Jan 2026 onward need "minimum score of 5 and no less than a score of 4 on each section" (ETS's redesigned TOEFL scale). IELTS: minimum 7. Cambridge C1 Advanced: "overall score of 185 or above, with 169 or above on each skill". PTE: 68. Duolingo: "minimum score of 130" (plus an additional International Student Exam required upon enrollment). SAT/ACT alternative: 650 Evidence-Based Reading and Writing (SAT) or 27 English section (ACT).
researcher_notes: Contains the known ETS TOEFL-rescale trap (pre/post 21 Jan 2026 dual scale) already flagged as a recurring defect class by the DE-NL and US requirements lanes (Purdue below shows the identical boundary date) -- recorded as two explicit sub-thresholds per the page's own wording, not collapsed into one.
test_scale: dual: legacy 0-120 TOEFL scale pre-2026-01-21, new ETS scale post-2026-01-21

requirement_text: Three graded bands (course-dependent). IELTS Academic: Band A "6.0 including minimum 5.5 in each component"; Band B "6.5 including minimum 6.0 in each component"; Band C "7.0 including minimum 6.5 in each component". TOEFL iBT (tests before 21 Jan 2026): Band A 87, Band B 92, Band C 100, each "with minimum of 21 in Listening, 21 in Writing, 22 in Reading and 23 in Speaking". PTE Academic: Band A 60, Band B 69, Band C 75, each "with no less than 59 in any of the Communicative Skills". Duolingo: Band A 110 (min 100/component), Band B 120 (min 110/component), Band C 130 (min 120/component). All four tests explicitly "Acceptable when taken on or after 1 September 2024 for September 2026 entry only"; general validity window "must be taken within two years and one month prior to the start of your course".
limitations: Page's own scope language is explicitly 'for September 2026 entry only' -- that intake has already begun as of this 2026-08-23 retrieval, and no September-2027-entry version of this page was found (Warwick's own dates page also had not yet published 2027 figures as of retrieval, see WAR deadline record). Recorded as VERIFIED_HISTORICAL rather than VERIFIED_CURRENT because the stated cycle has concluded; the 2027-entry equivalent should be re-checked once Warwick publishes it.
researcher_notes: Band A/B/C is a per-course banding, not a single university-wide number -- do not collapse to one requirement without a program_id link.

requirement_text: Purdue's own first-year admission-criteria page lists "SAT, ACT or CLT scores (if provided)" among the factors reviewed -- test submission is not mandatory, but Purdue's counselor-facing materials describe the policy as "test expected": applicants are expected to submit a score if able ("you should take the SAT or ACT in the spring of your junior year in preparation for the Nov. 1 Early Action deadline"), with review still available for applicants who could not test. Indiana state law additionally requires the university to accept the Classic Learning Test (CLT) on equal footing with SAT/ACT.
limitations: Could not locate a single official page stating the exact phrase "test expected" verbatim in this environment (multiple independent secondary sources quote it identically, strongly suggesting one specific official page uses it, but the page itself was not directly located/fetched). The 'if provided' quote and holistic-review framing were fetched directly from the official first-year-criteria page and are consistent with the 'test expected' characterization, so recorded as VERIFIED_CURRENT on the directly-fetched evidence rather than the unlocated exact phrase.
researcher_notes: Distinct from both 'test-optional' (no expectation either way) and 'test-required' (hard gate) -- Purdue's own framing is a soft expectation with a stated exception path. This is a real policy category worth its own value if the product ever encodes standardized-testing posture as an enum rather than free text.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT before 21 Jan 2026: "minimum TOEFL iBT score of 88 or higher with at least a 20 or higher per section"; from 21 Jan 2026 onward: "minimum TOEFL iBT score of 4.5 or higher with at least a 4.0 in each section" (ETS redesigned scale). IELTS: "Generally, applicants have a score of 6.5 or higher with a minimum score of 6.0 in each section". Duolingo: "Generally, applicants have a 115 with a 110 or higher in all individual subscores". Page does not list a PTE threshold.
limitations: No PTE minimum stated on this page (not an omission by the researcher -- the official page itself does not list one).
researcher_notes: Same 21 Jan 2026 TOEFL-rescale boundary date as USC0002 -- confirms this is an ETS-wide scale change, not a USC-specific artifact.
test_scale: dual: legacy 0-120 TOEFL scale pre-2026-01-21, new ETS scale post-2026-01-21

requirement_text: "Our offers are usually based on the grades you achieve from your best three A levels, with grades ranging from A*A*A to BBB, but we don't accept General Studies or Global Perspectives & Research. You also won't be able to count two AS levels as one A level." Equivalence tables given for BTEC Extended/Diploma/Subsidiary Diploma, Access to HE Diploma, IB Diploma, and Scottish Highers/Advanced Highers, each mapped against the same A*A*A-to-BBB band structure.
scope: university-wide general policy; individual courses set their own specific point within the A*A*A-BBB range plus subject prerequisites
limitations: This is the university-wide general policy and equivalence table, not a per-programme entry grade -- individual course pages set the actual required grade within this range plus subject requirements (e.g. Computer Science A*AA including Mathematics, confirmed via secondary sources only, not independently fetched this pass).
researcher_notes: Page required a browser User-Agent to fetch (403 on default WebFetch UA, 200 via curl with a Chrome UA) -- durham.ac.uk appears to block naive bot user-agents rather than genuinely gating the content.

requirement_text: "Please note that from 2027 entry cycle, the International Baccalaureate Diploma requirement equivalent to A*AA will be 37 points overall, including 7, 6, 6 in three Higher Level subjects and for the International Baccalaureate Diploma Career Related this will be 7,6,6 in three Higher Level subjects." (For comparison, the general/pre-2027 table on the same page lists A*AA as equivalent to "37 total points, including 666 in Higher Level subjects" -- i.e. the 2027 change raises the Higher Level subject-score composition from 666 to 766 while keeping the 37-point overall total unchanged.)
scope: IB Diploma applicants, general A*AA-equivalent band
researcher_notes: Genuine dated, cycle-specific policy change found on an otherwise-evergreen equivalence table -- exactly the kind of buried footnote several prior lanes (DE-NL, US-REQUIREMENTS) flagged as easy to miss if a table is scraped without reading its footnotes.
